tagline: North through the chapters, from Many Farms to Mexican Water.
intro: US 191 runs north from Many Farms across open high desert on the Navajo Nation, over Chinle Wash, Lukachukai Wash and the other washes that cut across the corridor, among high sandstone buttes. Hogans, shade houses and corrals stand here and there, and livestock graze along the roadside.

The road passes through Round Rock and Rock Point and ends at US 160 near Mexican Water. Its name, Tsé Nikání, flat mesa rock, belongs to the mesa west of Round Rock and serves as that town's Navajo name too.

moments.title: Many Farms
moments.text: The name is a plain translation of the Navajo, and the farms were fully irrigated by 1937. Off the road, Many Farms Lake holds 25,000 acre-feet.

moments.title: Round Rock
moments.text: Its trading post on Lukachukai Wash dates from 1887, the first in the region by one early account. Birders have seen well over 200 species at the nearby lake, one year including swans.

moments.title: Rock Point
moments.text: Named for the point where Chinle Creek enters high sandstone walls. Its first name, standing metal, came from a windmill.
